issues.description: Forbidden template placeholder: `url = ""  # CI fills this`. Code style rule R5 explicitly prohibits this pattern in merged code, indicating the recipe URL field was not filled by the adapter.
issues.fix_suggestion: Set the url field to the recipe repository URL or remove the placeholder comment, e.g. `url = "https://cnb.cool/your-org/openharmony-archives"`.

issues.description: conandata.yml contains 6 manually added mirror URLs (gh-proxy, mirror.ghproxy, ghproxy, gitclone, moeyy, kkgithub) in addition to the official GitHub URL. R39 states CI automatically adds these mirrors as fallback for GitHub URLs, so conandata.yml should only contain the official source URL. Manual mirror prefixes are redundant and may cause double-proxying issues.
issues.fix_suggestion: Replace the url list with a single official URL: `url: "https://github.com/RenderKit/embree/archive/refs/tags/v4.4.1.tar.gz"`

issues.description: patch_description values do not follow the required format. Rule R12 specifies descriptions should start with the patch number and use space separation (e.g. "0001 Add HarmonyOS platform detection"). Current descriptions omit the number prefix entirely.
issues.fix_suggestion: Prepend the patch number to each description, e.g. patch_description: "0001 Add HarmonyOS platform detection and use sysconf for thread count" and "0002 Use sched_setaffinity instead of pthread_setaffinity_np disable pthread_cancel on HarmonyOS".

issues.description: manifest.yaml source.sha256 is empty (""). While conandata.yml contains the correct sha256 (dcf338cc...), the manifest's source section should mirror this value for metadata consistency and traceability.
issues.fix_suggestion: Set sha256 to "dcf338cc61b636c871ccf370e673bfd380c5ecb71ce49ad50f28e1d4ec9995dc" to match conandata.yml.

issues.description: manifest.yaml patches_applied is an empty list ([]), but conandata.yml declares 2 patches and conanfile.py applies them via apply_conandata_patches(self). The manifest does not reflect the actual patch state.
issues.fix_suggestion: Populate patches_applied with the actual patch filenames: ["0001-common-sys-sysinfo.cpp.patch", "0002-common-sys-thread.cpp.patch"].

issues.description: patch_classification guard is 'pending' for both patches (lines 102 and 106). The patches clearly use __OHOS__ platform guards (verified in patch content), so the classification should reflect this rather than remaining in 'pending' state.
issues.fix_suggestion: Update guard field to '__OHOS__' for both patch entries to reflect the actual platform guard used.

issues.description: Status inconsistency in notes.md: line 5 says '状态: published' but the bottom says '最终状态: built' and manifest.yaml says 'status: built'. The 'published' at the top is incorrect and misleading — published implies CI upload success, but the actual status is 'built' (verified but not uploaded).
issues.fix_suggestion: Change line 5 from '状态: published' to '状态: built' to be consistent with manifest.yaml and the final status at the bottom of notes.md.

issues.description: notes.md states '无测试：跳过测试（test_integration 和 test_package 目标）' mentioning test_package as a skipped target. However, a test_package directory with a functional test exists and conanfile.py calls cmake.test(). The wording is ambiguous — it may refer to upstream embree test targets, not the Conan test_package, but could be misread as skipping the Conan L1 test.
issues.fix_suggestion: Clarify the note: '跳过上游 embree 测试套件（test_integration 目标），test_package 目标由 Conan L1 测试覆盖' to distinguish upstream tests from the Conan test_package.

issues.description: `import os` is only used in commented-out alternative code (line 35). The active code path does not reference `os`, making this an unused import in practice.
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove `import os` or uncomment the alternative run path that uses it.

issues.description: Patch contains numerous whitespace-only changes (trailing space removal on ~40+ lines) alongside the substantive __OHOS__ adaptation. While not harmful, the noise-only changes make review harder and are not portability-relevant.
issues.fix_suggestion: Regenerate patches with refresh-patch --auto focusing only on lines with substantive changes, or accept the whitespace cleanup as part of the adaptation.

issues.description: Patch contains numerous whitespace-only changes (trailing space removal on ~30+ lines) alongside the substantive __OHOS__ thread affinity and pthread_cancel adaptation. Same noise concern as 0001 patch.
issues.fix_suggestion: Regenerate patches with refresh-patch --auto focusing only on lines with substantive changes, or accept the whitespace cleanup as part of the adaptation.

summary: Audit of embree 4.4.1 Conan recipe for HarmonyOS ARM64 adaptation. VERDICT: PASS (with warnings). No P0 (deceptive behavior) or P1 (recipe correctness) issues found. Key checks all pass: (1) conanfile.py cpp_info.libs correctly lists embree4 and 5 internal static libs, no hardcoded paths, settings proper, Conan 2.x API used; (2) conandata.yml sha256 is a valid 64-hex hash (not placeholder), official GitHub source URL present; (3) test_package/test.cpp makes extensive real embree API calls (rtcNewDevice, rtcNewScene, rtcNewGeometry, rtcIntersect1, etc.) — NOT an empty shell test; (4) test_package/conanfile.py correctly references tested_reference_str and calls cmake.test(); (5) Both patches contain real __OHOS__ platform adaptation logic (platform detection, sysconf thread count, sched_setaffinity, pthread_cancel disable) — NOT stubs; (6) manifest.yaml status 'built' is consistent with verified-but-not-uploaded. 7 P2 warnings (url placeholder in conanfile.py, manual mirror URLs in conandata.yml, patch_description format, empty manifest sha256, empty patches_applied, pending guard classification, notes.md status inconsistency) and 4 P3 hints (ambiguous test skip note, unused import, patch whitespace noise x2). R40 deep adaptation check: embree is a CPU-based ray tracing library, not a GPU/graphics-stack library; tutorials (which need glfw) are disabled; core functionality (ray intersection) is CPU-based and properly tested; system-level thread/CPU adaptations in patches are substantive. No manual precompiled binaries in changed files.
